NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for
  viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday following the
  meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 835 1475 9262, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 835 1475 9262, Meeting Password: 066081
  Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
  following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand"
  option at the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which
  item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 23, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:04 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Dev/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

Carmelo Sorce from Cal Water provided an update on the Palos Verdes Pipeline Project,
reporting that almost all seven miles of pipelines are now tied-in, with the final tie-in
occurring tomorrow. The pump station is 95% complete, and expected to be fully
complete in approximately one month. The full project completion is targeted for August.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  ZUCKERMAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-I AS FOLLOWS
  BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  APPROVED.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the

platforms. No public testimony was received.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  FY 2020-21 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing and take any
  public testimony related to the budget adoption including appropriation limit, fees &
  charges, fund balance policy and investment policy; 2) close the Public Hearing; and
  3) review and adopt Resolutions 2454, 2455, and 2456, Statement of Fund Balance
  Policy, and Statement of Investment Policy.

  City Manager Grammer provided an introduction and summary of the proposed FY
  2020-21 Budget, stating that the budget is a balanced budget with a General Fund
  Operating surplus of 2%, and includes a decrease in sales tax revenue and generally
  stable property tax and business license revenue. Building permit revenue is lower
  but still exceeds the historical average. The budget complies with the City Council’s
  Fund Balance Policy, maintaining a $1.2 million Emergency Reserve, with an
  additional $813,000 Contingency Reserve, totaling 25% of the General Fund
  operating expenditures in an unassigned fund balance reserve.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the
  agenda material).

  MAYOR SCHMITZ stated for the record that the Budget Study Session occurred on
  June 9, 2020 in an open public meeting, available to view on the City’s website, in
  which the Council thoroughly reviewed the budget.

C.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER (VERBAL
  REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the latest Los Angeles County Health Officer
Order, which as of last week has allowed for the reopening of nail salons, hair salons, spas,
massage therapy, tattoo/piercing shops, tanning salons, card rooms, bars and wineries. The
County has not yet allowed for the reopening of movie theaters, concert venues and youth
sports, but does allow for day camps which can include youth sport practices/training but no
games. Last week the Governor mandated face coverings be worn throughout the State,
which is consistent with the County’s Order. Daily confirmed cases has been rising, however
death rates have been lower overall. City staff has been exploring options to hold hybrid City
Council meetings, in-person and through Zoom, but have not found any viable options due
to technical problems, and will continue to research options.
